classification.difficultyReason: Model a fixed rectangular area by inverse variation, then filter whole-number factor pairs using the minimum wall length.

content.prompt: [Inverse Variation] An architect is designing a building. The client has insisted that one of the rooms in the building must have an area of $48\text{ m}^2$. For ease of design, the length $\ell$ and the breadth $b$ must each be a whole number of metres. Because of the furniture that must go into the room, no wall may be less than $4\text{ m}$. What are the possible dimensions of the room?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\ell b&=48\\b&=\frac{48}{\ell}\end{align*}$$
The positive whole-number factor pairs of $48$ are $(1,48)$, $(2,24)$, $(3,16)$, $(4,12)$ and $(6,8)$. Both dimensions must be at least $4\text{ m}$, so the possible dimensions are $4\text{ m}\times12\text{ m}$ or $6\text{ m}\times8\text{ m}$. Interchanging length and breadth gives the same room dimensions.
